title: Folic acid: fortification of flour with folic acid
journal: GOV.UK guidance, collection first published 24 January 2018, page updated 10 July 2026
result: Non-wholemeal wheat flour will be fortified by law with folic acid at 0.25 mg per 100 g from December 2026, with some products containing it from autumn 2025. Fortification is estimated to reduce neural tube defect rates in the UK by around 20%. Mandatory fortification will be in addition to foods already voluntarily fortified, such as many breakfast cereals; wholemeal flour, gluten-free products and other flours remain unfortified. Advice to take 400 µg folic acid daily from before conception until at least week 12 of pregnancy continues. Mandatory fortification was first recommended by the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition in 2006. The page states that, based on the available evidence, adding folic acid to flour is not associated with health concerns, and that the Food Standards Agency found no reports of hypersensitivity to folic acid in food.
